gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, gross profit increased by approximately $3.4 million, or 263%, to approximately $4.7 million compared to approximately $1.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 as a result of higher sales revenue in the current quarter. For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, gross margin increased to 34% from 29% in the quarter ended September 30, 2025. This five percentage point increase in gross profit margin was primally driven by better purchase economics on higher purchase volumes. Additionally, there was significantly increased DTC sales in the quarter compared to the prior year, which have a higher gross margin than the retail business. The Company intends to continue to focus on additional opportunities to reduce product costs & freight and warehousing costs.

sm.heading: Selling and Marketing Expenses
sm.text: Selling and marketing expenses for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 were approximately $2.3 million, an increase of approximately $1.3 million, or 130%, from approximately $1.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. This increase was primarily a result of an increase in broker and royalty payments related to Fallout product sales. Selling and marketing expenses as a percentage of revenue decreased to 17.0% in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 from 22.5% in the same period in 2025. We intend to continue to look for clear return on investment from our selling and marketing expenses to drive profitable sales. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, non-cash expenses included in selling and marketing expenses (stock compensation and depreciation) were approximately $0.1 million and $0.0 million, respectively.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 were approximately $2.0 million compared to $1.7 million in the quarter ended September 30, 2025 or an increase of $0.3 million. This increase was primary related to increased salary and benefits during the current quarter compared to the same quarter in 2025. General and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue decreased to 14.5% in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 from 37.5% in the same quarter in 2025. We intend to continue to look for additional opportunities to reduce our G&A costs. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, non-cash expenses included in general and administrative expenses (stock compensation and depreciation) were approximately $0.4 million and $0.4 million, respectively.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text: Net Income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was approximately $0.5 million compared to net loss of approximately $1.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, an improvement of $1.9 million. This increase in net income was primarily attributable to higher gross profit and selling, general, and administrative expenses being a much lower percentage of revenue as compared to the prior year.

ocf.text: Although the Company generated net income during the third quarter of 2026 and improved its cash balance and working capital position, it has a history of operating losses and negative cash flows from operating activities. Management continues to pursue initiatives to improve operating performance and liquidity, including strengthening core beverage distribution, pursuing consumer lifestyle and functional health opportunities, controlling operating costs, and managing working capital. The Company also maintains a $10.0 million credit facility with Two Shores Capital Corp. (the “Credit Facility”), under which advances bear interest at 13.75% per annum. All present and future obligations of the Loan Subsidiary under the 2Shores Loan Credit Facility are secured by a first-priority security interest in all assets of the Company, the Loan Subsidiary, and the Company’s other U.S. subsidiaries. The amount of additional borrowing capacity, if any, is subject to the Credit Facility’s terms and applicable borrowing conditions. Notwithstanding improvements in financial performance and management’s plans, substantial doubt remains regarding the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the issuance date of the financial statements, as further discussed in Note 1 to the condensed consolidated financial statements.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, and December 31, 2025, the Company had cash of approximately $4.4 million and $3.6 million, respectively, and working capital (deficiency) of approximately $2.1 million and ($0.5 million), respectively. The Company reported a net loss from continuing operations of approximately $0.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net income from continuing operations of approximately $0.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s accumulated deficit increased to approximately $94.8 million, compared to approximately $94.7 million as of December 31, 2025.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased by approximately $9.2 million, or 205%, to approximately $13.7 million compared to approximately $4.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase in sales revenue was primarily the result of Fallout branded products sold through our club and DTC channels. HD9 Sales declined from $0.8M to $0.0M due to federal hemp THC ban that comes into effect December 11, 2026 in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025. The company expects to cease all HD9 product sales in the fourth quarter prior to the ban coming into effect December 11, 2026.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, trade spend and promotional allowances, which reduced the amount of revenue for the sales of our product, totaled approximately $1.6 million, an increase of approximately $0.9 million, or 128%, compared to approximately $0.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily driven trade spend associated with our Fallout branded products sold through our club channel.

intro.text: Jones Soda Co. develops, produces, markets and distributes premium beverages that we sell and distribute primarily in the United States and Canada through our network of independent distributors and directly to our national and regional retail accounts. We also sell products in select international markets. Our products are sold in grocery stores, convenience and gas stores, on fountain in restaurants, “up and down the street” in independent accounts such as delicatessens, sandwich shops and burger restaurants, as well as through our national accounts with several large retailers. We refer to our network of independent distributors as our direct store delivery (“DSD”) channel, and we refer to our national and regional accounts who receive shipments directly from us as our direct to retail (“DTR”) channel.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, sales in the United States represented approximately 88% of total sales, while sales in Canada represented approximately 12%.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024 one customer accounted for approximately 31% and nil% of total revenues.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, and 2024 a second customer accounted for approximately 4% and 13% of total revenues.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, our two largest customers accounted for approximately 31.2% and 4.1% of our total revenues, respectively, and in the aggregate represented approximately 35.3% of our total revenues.

For the year ended December 31, 2024, our two largest customers accounted for approximately 18.8% and 5.8% of our total revenues, respectively, and in the aggregate represented approximately 24.6% of our total revenues.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 39% of our total net revenue was attributable to products utilizing one or more licensed properties, including the licensed property, Fallout.
These two channels accounted for 35% of 2025 gross sales compared to 5.6% in 2024.

As of December 31, 2025, one customer accounted for approximately 44 % of our accounts receivable, whereas as of December 31, 2024, no individual customer represented a material concentration of our accounts receivable.
Net sales generated in the United States accounted for 89 % and 83 % of total revenue during the year ended December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

The amount of additional capital we may require, the timing of our capital needs and the availability of financing to fund those needs will depend on a number of factors, including our strategic initiatives and operating plans, the performance of our business and the market conditions for debt or equity financing.
Additionally, the amount of capital required will depend on our ability to meet our sales revenue goals and otherwise successfully execute our operating plan.
In addition, our business depends on acceptance by our independent distributors and retailers of our brands as beverage brands that have the potential to provide incremental sales growth.
Our success depends on our ability to maintain brand image for our existing products and effectively build up brand image for new products and brand extensions.
The success of this network will depend on the performance of the distributors, retailers and brokers of this network.
Our ability to maintain and expand our distribution network and attract additional distributors, retailers and brokers will depend on a number of factors, some of which are outside our control.
We depend on a limited number of significant customers for a substantial portion of our revenue.
Our inventory supply depends on our ability to correctly estimate demand for our products.
Our business relies on third-party transportation providers and logistics networks to deliver our products and materials.
We rely upon our ongoing relationships with our key flavor suppliers.
If we are unable to source our flavors on acceptable terms from our key suppliers, we could suffer disruptions in our business.
Our success depends on our ability to attract and retain highly qualified employees in such areas as finance, sales, marketing and product development.
We rely on a combination of trademark and trade secrecy laws, confidentiality procedures and contractual provisions to protect our intellectual property rights.
We depend upon licensed intellectual property to generate some our revenues.
Accordingly, investors must be prepared to rely on sales of their shares after price appreciation to earn an investment return, which may never occur.
